proposal.title: sys.counter: counter numbers kept as blocks, opt-in per counter
proposal.author: Giovanni Porcari

problem.p: A recycling counter (recycle=True) keeps its free numbers in the holes Bag of its adm.counter record. The Bag is a second copy of what the document table already says and drifts from it (genropy/genropy#1879); alignSequences rebuilds it, rewriting documents with fix_duplicate.

The goal is a numbering service, at the level of the sys package, whose state is easy to keep consistent and to query, and which keeps the API of a counter: counter_<field>(record), assignCounterColumn, releaseCounterColumn, guessCounter.

current.fact: The SQL layer calls trigger_assignCounters on insert and update (line 259) and trigger_releaseCounters on delete (line 319); their base versions are empty.

gnrdbo overrides those triggers and calls adm.counter from assignCounterColumn, releaseCounterColumn, guessCounter and _sequencesOnLoading: four call sites, the only ones that pick the numbering table.
Package adm requires gnrcore:sys; sys had no table named counter or counter_block.
current.p: genropy/genropy#1888 implemented the same block model inside adm; its review (fporcari, 2026-11-14) found four bugs and the overlap with adm.counter and genropy/genropy#1882. This proposal is the alternative to it.

section.title: Tables

list.item: sys.counter: one row per counter (pkg, tbl, fld, code), with no period. Its row is the lock of every operation on the counter.

sys.counter_block: one row per block, with the period of the block. A block is a run of consecutive numbers, occupied or free, with order_first and order_last: the order key of its first and last number; for a free block, those of the occupied numbers around it.

section.p: Order keys are integers that sort as the values: YYYYMMDD for a date, milliseconds since the epoch in UTC for a timestamp. A free number for a value is a plain query on sys.counter_block.
Work happens on the current period, so a lock per counter instead of per period changes little: only saves on other periods wait for it.

table.title: Keys of counter_<field>() in the new model

row.cell: Required when the format holds a period: it decides the period of the record.
Optional. The numbers follow its order: dates for a D column, the timestamp for DH/DHZ. Missing: the order is the date_field, as with adm.counter.
As with adm.counter: without order_field, no order is checked.
Requires an order: order_field, or a date_field without date_tolerant.

Default True. When false, a record going back to draft keeps its number. counter_<field>(record) may compute it from the record. Read by gnrdbo.trigger_releaseCounters, so it holds for adm.counter too.

list.item: New number: the lowest free number whose window holds the record's order key, for a recycling counter; otherwise the last number of the period plus one.
Number set by hand (insert, or changed on update): it splits the block that holds it; refused if occupied or outside its window. A value that is not a number of the series is left alone.

Release: the number becomes free and merges with free neighbours; a split reads the order key of the two new edges from the table. A neighbour missing from the table becomes an open bound and is left to checkCounter.
A number changed or cleared on update releases the old one in the period of the stored record. trigger_assignCounters passes old_record.

A period without blocks is loaded from the numbers already in the table, under the lock, the first time it is used. For a counter that does not recycle, the numbers adm.counter gave above the highest one still in the table stay occupied: a number deleted at the tail is never given again. A period whose numbers are inconsistent is refused, naming analyzeCounter.
The counter row is created with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING: two first saves of a counter do not fail, and no failed statement rolls back the save.
Guess (guessCounter, showOnLoad): a record not inserted yet takes now as a missing timestamp; with a missing date it is not recycled.

section.title: Switch
section.p: experimentalValue('new_counters', 'counters'): a list of pkg.table.field sends those counters to sys.counter; * sends every counter except a recycling one without an order, which stays on adm.counter. A listed recycling counter without an order is a configuration error. gnrdbo.sysCounter(field, record) makes the choice; adm.counter is not changed.

analyzeCounter, loadCounter and checkCounter report, load and verify every period of a counter; freeSequences lists the free numbers of a period with their window. checkCounter reports not_loaded for a period without blocks, blocks_differ for a recycling counter whose blocks differ from the table, and missing_from_blocks for a counter that does not recycle when a number of the table is not occupied in the blocks.

decision.question: Where does the numbering service live?
One header per period or per counter?

option.title: One per counter; the period on the blocks
Change the four call sites of gnrdbo
A service called from write.py; guessCounter and _sequencesOnLoading would still need gnrdbo

list.item: Code that calls adm.counter.assignCounter directly keeps numbering in adm.counter.
Turning the switch off sends the counter back to adm.counter, whose counter and holes do not know the numbers given meanwhile: alignSequences rebuilds them.
Writes that skip the Python triggers can still make the blocks drift; checkCounter reports it.
